assumptions: Everything in this scenario is simulated. No number here is a measurement of a real cluster.

Site capacities (power cap, cooling capacity, import limit) are scenario choices; the per-GPU accelerator fields follow the e001 screening scenario H100 SXM sites (experiments/e001-beyond-one-datacenter/screening-scenario-v1.json).

Compute-phase GPU power is 0.8 x the cited H100 SXM TDP (700 W): the 0.8 is the gpu_stack calculator's gpu_power_fraction assumption. Host overhead is 0.25 x compute power: the calculator's server_power_fraction assumption.

Idle/compute and relative compute-phase noise are measured ratios from the e002 laptop RTX telemetry. The communication-phase and checkpoint levels are set equal to the measured idle ratio (structural assumption, no measurement). The measured checkpoint/compute ratio is reported alongside in the result.
Fraction of a training step spent in compute (0.7) is an assumption.

Rack heat capacity per GPU = DGX H100 system mass 130.45 kg / 8 GPUs x an assumed effective specific heat of 500 J/(kg K). Mass source: https://docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgxh100-user-guide/introduction-to-dgxh100.html

Supply setpoint 24 C is an assumption inside the DGX H100 cited operating range of 5-30 C (same source). Design air rise 12 K, cooling lag 120 s, outdoor coupling 0.2 K/K above 30 C, capacity derate 1 percent per K above 30 C, GPU-to-air offset 0.05 K/W, protective GPU shutdown at 95 C and its 1800 s hold are assumptions.
Throttle threshold 80 C, span 8 K, minimum clock 0.5 and power exponent 2 are assumptions; they are not H100 datasheet values.

Cooling power: Carnot-shaped COP with second-law efficiency chosen so the overhead equals the gpu_stack calculator PUE assumption (1.2) at 20 C outdoor and 24 C supply; approach temperatures 10 K and COP bounds 1.5 to 30 are assumptions.

Breaker curve: IEC 60898-1 conventional values (1.13 and 1.45 x rated, 1 hour), https://www.se.com/au/en/faqs/FA369327/. Rack breaker ratings are 1.1 x the full-load rack power; reset delay 1800 s is an assumption.
WAN, restore, restart and membership parameters come from the e001 scenarios; the per-GPU checkpoint size is the e001 screening checkpoint (1.12 TB) divided by its 256 GPUs.
The job mix, outdoor temperature (including the heat wave), electricity price and carbon intensity are synthetic and seeded. Job value per GPU-hour is a synthetic number with no source.
Event precursors (supply-temperature creep, resistance rise, GPU temperature creep, breaker derate ramp, curtailment announcement) are assumptions of the simulation, not measured facts.
simplifications: Job admission, GPU clocks, thermal integration, breaker state, event onsets and controller decisions are evaluated at control-step boundaries; event onsets take effect at the first boundary at or after the stated time.
Thermal integration uses the mean rack power over each control step.
A synchronous job runs at the clock of its slowest GPU and all its GPUs are modeled at that clock.
Per-GPU power noise is independent across GPUs and seconds, scaled to the measured relative standard deviation of laptop compute-phase power.
GPU temperature uses the rack air temperature at the start of the control step and the previous step's mean GPU power.
Multi-site jobs take no separate checkpoints; their durable state is the last exact average.
A faulted GPU draws 0 W until repaired; its host stays powered unless the rack breaker is open.
